title: Real-Time Dynamic IR-drop Prediction for IR ECO
problem: During IR Engineering Change Order (ECO) stages in chip design, cell moving causes unpredictable IR-drop changes, requiring designers to run expensive simulations for each ECO candidate to evaluate voltage integrity, making design iterations slow.
motivation: Fast IR-drop prediction during ECO enables rapid design iteration and convergence, critical for meeting tight design schedules in advanced technology nodes.
method: When chip designers move cells, the resulting voltage drop becomes unpredictable. This approach trains a machine learning model (XGBoost) on examples of cell movements and their voltage effects, using the electrical context around each cell to predict outcomes. Instead of running expensive simulations (SPICE) that take over an hour each, the model predicts voltage impact in minutes, letting designers test multiple placement options in the same design session.
key_novelty: An XGBoost machine learning model predicts voltage drop immediately after moving cells in chip design, replacing hour-long simulation runs and enabling designers to test multiple placement options in parallel.
contributions: XGBoost IR-drop predictor with global cell-neighborhood context
Real-time dynamic IR-drop estimation (minutes vs. hour+ simulations)
64x speedup over traditional ML predictors with 93% detection accuracy
limitations: Evaluated on a single industrial 3nm design with 5 ECO candidates; generalization to other designs and technology nodes not clearly established.
primary_theme: ML-based real-time IR-drop prediction for ECO acceleration
